findings.reason: the plan must name where the pol_angle_like class lives (ambix owns the factor table, or nova gains it), otherwise the angle-binding node has no implementable target.
findings.text: `canonical_factor` is a two-line delegate to `nova.io.cocos.transform_factor`; §6 says to give "the COCOS transform factors" a `pol_angle_like` class at that resolver, but the resolver owns no table, so the change is unimplementable where the plan says it. Editing nova's table is closed off by §7's "nothing JT-60SA-specific is added to nova", and the plan never states that ambix must stop delegating and own the table itself — a distinction the first implementing node cannot resolve on its own

findings.reason: the plan should extend the mechanism it declared as the angle selector (`_supply_declared_probe_angles` / the `description` branch of `read_geometry_table`) rather than add a parallel read in the adapter, or state why that slot cannot carry it.
findings.text: `_b_probes` hard-sets `angle_deg=float("nan")`, and `read_geometry_table` (description_reader.py:144) already routes angle supply through the catalogue's `probe_angle_source`, filling MAST's under `_supply_declared_probe_angles` and applying nothing for `"description"`. §4 introduced that slot and `jt-60sa.json` declares `description`, yet §6's fix (c) reads the emitted angle in the adapter instead of completing the owner's `description` branch, so the slot §4 built governs nothing on the JT-60SA route and two angle-supply mechanisms end up keyed off the same one selector

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new entry points each hide substantial behaviour behind a small interface (measure_convention hides the Grad–Shafranov integral and sign tests; the SELENE/EQDB loaders return one typed record the existing kernels already read), rather than spreading complexity across parallel wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan puts the probe-angle read in `geometry_adapter._b_probes` while `description_reader._supply_declared_probe_angles` is already the angle-supply owner selected by the catalogue's `probe_angle_source` slot.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every section that adds surface states in its own text what it retires or why nothing can be (measure_convention "retires nothing, because no generic convention entry exists"; the EQDB request/record types "retire nothing, because no equilibrium-database request type exists"; --machine "replaces the implicit MAST default ... retires nothing else"), and §5 adds no public definition or refusal family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names the existing owner for every mechanism it adds (description_reader.read_geometry_table, data/cocos_convention.score_convention, challenge/convention._integrated_current, eval/efit_referee.judge_geometry, data/eddb.py writers, gs/artifact_resolution pins, spine_bench/shots.resolve_shotset_version) and cites the search behind each; the one omission is carried as the thin_wrapper finding below.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §6 asks `imas_ambix/cocos.py` `canonical_factor` to gain a `pol_angle_like` class where the COCOS factors are resolved, but `canonical_factor` holds no factor table: it forwards to `nova.io.cocos.transform_factor`.
